stem: A network performance study measures the download speed (Mbps) for a sample of 30 subscribers. The sample mean is 441.2 Mbps with a sample standard deviation of 157.9 Mbps. However, 2 of the 30 observations appear to be outliers (values more than 2.5 standard deviations from the mean). If these outliers are removed, the remaining 28 observations have a mean of 412.1 Mbps and standard deviation of 95.2 Mbps. Estimate the true population mean and provide a 95% confidence interval that accounts for the uncertainty about whether outliers should be included.

ground_truth.answer: With all data: mean = 441.2, 95% CI = [382.2, 500.2]. Without outliers: mean = 412.1, 95% CI = [376.1, 448.1]. Combined interval accounting for analytic uncertainty: [376.1, 500.2]. Point estimate: 426.6 Mbps.

solution_steps: The outlier treatment choice creates structural uncertainty. Combined interval: [376.1, 500.2].
common_failure_modes: Using only the full sample without considering outlier impact
Removing outliers without reporting both analyses
Not recognizing that the choice of analysis method is itself a source of uncertainty
